maya: Heads-up — ran a 24h long-session profiling run for INT8 KV with BF16-fallback after the recent kernel-selection change. Short summary: ~28% KV memory savings vs baseline, but tail perplexity on safety prompt set increased ~2.1%. Main signal is increased slot churn / fragmentation under mixed workloads. See gist: https://redwood-internal/gists/kv-longsession-171500

aj: Link?

maya: https://redwood-internal/gists/kv-longsession-171500 (main artifacts: kv_eviction_heatmap.png, kv_write_trace.data, sampling_table.csv)

liam: Did you compare against the pre-fused matmul kernel? i.e. old kernel vs fused kernel we switched to last week.

maya: Yes. Fused kernel + INT8 gives ~12% faster token throughput but we observe more non-sequential KV writes leading to fragmentation. Perf snippet we used:
```
perf record -e cpu-clock -o run.data -- ./serve --model rwd-7b --kv-mode=int8 --profile-kv
```
Key hotspot shows strided stores in the tiled kernel path.

sasha: Could the 2.1% perplexity regression be noise from eval sampling? or is it concentrated on specific prefixes?

aj: We ran eval A/B on curated prompt set. The regression concentrates on prompts with long repeated prefix tokens (system messages + long context). BF16-fallback (keep FP keys on first 4 layers) reduces PPL delta to ~0.3% but reduces memory savings to ~18%.

maya: Telemetry from 24h run: long sessions (>32k tokens) see slot reuse drop to ~0.6x baseline and eviction-rate spikes when concurrent small chats interleave. Example eviction log line: `EVICT slot=3942 reason=page_pressure resid=0.78`

liam: Sounds workload-dependent — interleaving multiple short chats and a single long chat could cause allocator to spread recently-touched slots. Are batching heuristics exacerbating this by scattering requests across GPU partitions?

maya: Yes. Current batching heuristics prioritize throughput and pack small micro-batches aggressively; that increases interleaving. Proposed mitigations: 1) coalesce slot writes in the kernel to preserve locality, 2) adaptive batching that keeps long-session affinity (favoring contiguous slot placement), 3) BF16 partial-fallback for keys in top-N layers as aj mentioned.

sasha: Agree. Option 1 is least invasive; if we can coalesce writes in the kernel we might retain most INT8 memory wins.

maya: I've pushed branch kv/coalesce-write-1715 with a write-coalescing micro-op. Canary script: `./run_canary.sh --duration=6h --profile=kv_write --workload=mixed_long_single` — route includes many small-chats + 1 long-chat (50k tokens). Logs go to /tmp/kv_canary.log on staging.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: started canary deployment kv/coalesce-write-1715 to staging at 1715005800

aj: I'll run the staging canary and grab 30m/6h snapshots, will post preliminary metrics in ~7h.

liam: Also double-check kernel memory fences and any implicit flushes on the tiled path — unnecessary fences break write locality and could explain the observed striding.

maya: Good call. Kernel selection notes: A100 uses kernel_X (global-store) by default; H100 has kernel_Y (tiled-store). We should prefer the tiled-store variant when using INT8 KV to improve write locality. I'll add selection hints in the kernel-table.

sasha: :thumbsup: Add perf charts to the perf doc and flag the 2.1% PPL regression in the rollforward checklist. If canary looks good, roll to 10% prod and monitor PPL + tail latency + kv_residency.

aj: Canary 30m update: eviction-rate down ~43%, effective KV memory saving ~26% (vs 28% earlier), PPL diff now ~0.4%. Snapshots: https://redwood-internal/snapshots/kv-canary-171500-30m

maya: Nice — that's promising. I'll open a perf PR with the coalesce patch and add a kernel selection guard. We'll keep BF16-fallback as a safety knob if we see any customer-facing regressions.

liam: If we go forward, let's add a telemetry metric for slot-contiguity (new metric) so we can guard future kernel swaps.

maya: Will do. Notes and artifacts saved to the gist and perf doc. Thanks all.
